statement: The Longhouse Religion (Gaihwi:io, "Good Message," also the Code of Handsome Lake) is a documented, relatively recent (early 19th-century) religious REFORM movement, not ancient tradition. Handsome Lake (Ganioʼdaiʼio/Sganyodaiyo), a Seneca leader, experienced visions beginning 1799 following a period of severe alcoholism and post-Revolutionary-War social collapse in Seneca communities (land loss, factionalism); three spiritual messengers reportedly delivered the code he then preached, explicitly combining older Haudenosaunee religious tradition with selected Christian influences in direct response to that specific social/political crisis. Anthony F.C. Wallace, The Death and Rebirth of the Seneca (Alfred A. Knopf, 1970), is the foundational academic treatment; Wallace reported roughly 5,000 practicing Gaihwi:io members as of 1969. This case is a documented parallel to the Yolŋu Elcho Island adjustment movement (Australia batch, Berndt 1962) — Indigenous-led religious innovation responding to colonial disruption, not externally imposed content nor primordial tradition.

sources.citation: Wallace, Anthony F.C. The Death and Rebirth of the Seneca. New York: Alfred A. Knopf, 1970.
sources.author: Anthony F.C. Wallace

does_not_demonstrate: That the Longhouse Religion is an unbroken continuation of pre-contact Haudenosaunee ceremonial practice rather than a documented early-19th-century reform synthesizing older tradition with Christian influence
